big_idea: CAPACITY = how much it HOLDS. MASS = how HEAVY. Different units = different counts.
learning_intention: We are learning to measure capacity and mass with non-standard units.
student_learning_goal: I can measure capacity and mass with non-standard units.
success_criteria: I can MEASURE capacity with cups or scoops.
I can MEASURE mass with a pan balance.
I can SHOW different units = different counts.
I can EXPLAIN gaps and overlaps.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Cal the Calendar Cat — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Pan Balance Cards (1 set per pair)
Capacity Cup Cards (1 set per pair)

minds_on.hook: Cal: CAPACITY tells how much a cup HOLDS. MASS tells how HEAVY a pumpkin is. Pour and weigh! Roo opens: 'CAPACITY for what FITS, MASS for what WEIGHS!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Cal the Calendar Cat puppet with stopwatch. 'Measurement friends — today we measure how much HOLDS (capacity) and how HEAVY (mass).'

Define. 'CAPACITY = HOW MUCH a container HOLDS. MASS = HOW HEAVY something is.'

Capacity demo. 'A pail. Fill with cups of water. 6 CUPS = capacity. 6 cups, but if SCOOPS (smaller) = 12 SCOOPS. SAME pail, different unit!'

'Cal says — different unit SIZES → different COUNTS. But the pail still holds the SAME water!'

That's E2.5 — same attribute, different units, different counts.

Mass demo. 'A pumpkin. Pan balance. 1 pumpkin balances 5 small rocks. Same pumpkin balances 1 BIG rock. Different units, different counts. Same mass.'

Now accuracy. 'When pouring, careful — DON'T overfill (counts too many) or underfill (counts too few). Same as area: gaps and overlaps cause errors.'

Demo overfill. 'Pour cup until water TOUCHES the rim, not OVER.'

'Cal says — accurate counts mean accurate measure!'

Now each pair gets Capacity Cards (5 containers with cup and scoop counts) + Pan Balance Cards (4 mass comparisons). They:
1. Compare 4 capacity cards (which holds more?).
2. Read 4 pan balance cards.

'Cal says — measure CAREFULLY!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Capacity Cards. Pairs compare 4 containers.
Hand out Pan Balance Cards. Pairs read 4 mass comparisons.
Stretch: same pail, count in cups AND in scoops.
STRATEGY COMPARE: Pairs predict the cup-to-scoop count for a NEW pail BEFORE pouring, then test. Class compares prediction-vs-actual. Cite Lehrer (2003) on measurement conservation.
steps.teacher_prompt: Cal: 'Predicting first SHARPENS your sense. Testing TELLS the truth.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Pour real cups in sink area. NO-MATERIALS PATH: teacher voices container scenarios; children predict by holding hands wider/narrower for capacity, thumbs-up/thumbs-down for heavier/lighter.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: capacity; mass; same-attribute; explains; consistency.

discussion_prompts: Why does cup count differ from scoop count?
consolidation.exit_routine: Roo+Cal mass+capacity refrain — 'Roo measures CAPACITY, Cal weighs MASS — same NUMBER, different ATTRIBUTE!' (3x). Each child predicts then tests one container.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says CUPS vs SCOOPS = different capacity — repairing the unit-vs-attribute trap at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On capacity + mass, the Grade-3 trap is conservation failure: child says 'taller container = more capacity' regardless of width (Lehrer 2003 length/measure conservation). Without conservation, predictions cannot ground.

Yesterday Lesson 3 introduced cm². Today: capacity + mass with standard units (mL, L, g, kg). Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capacity activity. Child says cup-count and scoop-count are 'different capacities'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Cal asks — is the WATER in the pail different?'

Probe. 'Same water. Same pail. Cup is BIGGER unit so fewer needed. Scoop is SMALLER unit so more needed. CAPACITY is the same.'

Generalise. 'Cal says — different UNITS give different COUNTS. The ATTRIBUTE (capacity) doesn't change.'

If still confused: pour 6 cups into 12 scoops. 'See — same water!'
common_misconceptions: Bigger count = more. (Repair: bigger count = smaller unit.)
Cup vs scoop = different attribute. (Repair: same attribute.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child says 'taller = more': pour visibly more into a wider, shorter container; child sees taller doesn't always mean more.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child uses scale but reads wrong: drill the decimal — 'kilogram = 1000 grams' as a benchmark.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can predict but cannot cite: force 'I predicted ___ because the cup holds about ___ mL.'

parts_outline.task: Compare 4 capacity card pairs (which holds more?).
Read 4 pan balance cards (heavier, lighter, equal).
If pail = 6 cups, how many scoops? (1 cup = 2 scoops)
